observations:
Torah #27 yields only one package in the current dataset. The source text was examined for any group of 3+ concepts sharing bechina-language that would form an independent domain not covered by Package 1.

Candidate 1 — ברית cluster: The text contains 'עזי זה בחינת ברית' and 'זה בחינת ברית' (referring to 'זה' in 'זה אלי ואנוהו'). These give us ברית equated with עז and with the demonstrative 'זה'. However, only 2 named concepts (עז and the Aramaic expression for ברית) form this cluster — insufficient for a standalone package (threshold: 3+ nodes). Furthermore, in this Torah, ברית functions primarily as the eitza prerequisite for הדרת פנים and קול, not as a parallel conceptual domain.

Candidate 2 — שלום cluster: שלום is the central goal/output of Torah #27. However, ALL שלום connections in the dataset are eitza (flows into שלום from prior conditions). The text does not equate שלום with anything else via bechina language — instead it says שלום is produced by הדרת פנים (eitza), is a healing medicine (metaphor), and is clothed in bitterness (מרירות). None of these constitute bechina equations. שלום therefore cannot form a bechina-based package.

Candidate 3 — שירה/זמרת/קול: These three are all bechina of קול (שירה=קול, זמרת=קול). They would form a sub-cluster, but since קול is already in Package 1 (the main package), they are additions to Package 1, not a separate independent package. Putting them in a new package would violate the 'every bechina-connected node in exactly one package' rule — they are connected to Package 1's dominant cluster through קול.

Candidate 4 — Evil mirror package: Torah #27 does contain a negative counterpart to the wisdom-radiance complex: the קנה רצוץ (crushed reed) and the nations (עכו"ם) who are 'far from זקן — זה קנה חכמה, from הדרת פנים, and cleave to קנה רצוץ' (source text section on 'רצוצא'). However, these appear only in eitza edges in the current dataset — no bechina edges encode an evil-polarity cluster for Torah 27. Without bechina edges, no evil-mirror package can be constituted from the existing dataset. (This is a dataset gap, not a structural absence — the text clearly implies such a mirror, with קנה רצוץ as the anti-זקן/anti-חכמה principle.)

Conclusion: With 3 bechina edges producing 1 package (after merge), and no independent group of 3+ bechina-connected nodes remaining outside that package, Torah #27 supports exactly one package in the current dataset. The apparent richness of the Torah's teaching is encoded primarily through its eitza chain: ברית → קול/הדרת פנים → שלום. The single package captures the conceptual identity-cluster that mediates this chain.
